_description: Universal Parts Consciousness - Material Interface Awareness
_purpose: Critical engineering documentation for material junctions in engines - where aluminum meets iron, steel meets aluminum, etc.

aluminum_block_iron_liner.description: Press-fit or cast-in iron cylinder liners in aluminum engine blocks

thermal_differential.engineering_impact: Aluminum expands nearly 2x faster than iron - critical for interference fit retention

interference_fit.purpose: Maintain contact at operating temperature despite differential expansion
interference_fit.failure_mode: Insufficient interference allows liner movement under combustion loads

liner_flange.purpose: Prevents axial movement and provides deck sealing surface
liner_flange.material_note: Flange contacts aluminum deck - requires controlled surface finish

heat_transfer_path.description: Heat must conduct from iron liner through interference fit to aluminum block to coolant
heat_transfer_path.gap_resistance: Air gap from lost interference creates thermal barrier - hotspots, detonation

overbore_limits.limiting_factor: Minimum wall thickness to parent material
overbore_limits.note: Unlike all-iron blocks, cannot bore significantly oversize

liner_replacement.feasibility: Possible but requires specialized pressing equipment
liner_replacement.deck_height_concern: Must verify deck height after liner replacement

thermal_cycling.concern: Repeated hot/cold cycles stress the interference fit
thermal_cycling.high_performance_note: Track use with extreme thermal cycles can loosen liners

failure_modes: Liner dropout from lost interference fit
Bore distortion from uneven thermal distribution
Cavitation erosion on coolant side of liner
engines_using_this_interface: BMW N54/N55/B58 (all modern BMW turbo engines)

aluminum_head_iron_block.description: Aluminum cylinder head mated to cast iron block - classic hybrid construction

thermal_differential.engineering_impact: Head grows significantly more than block - head bolts must accommodate this movement

head_gasket_requirements.composite_gasket_risk: Composite gaskets cannot reliably seal dissimilar expansion materials
mls_advantages: Spring steel layers accommodate differential movement
Embossed combustion seals maintain contact pressure

surface_finish_requirements.note: MLS gaskets require smoother surfaces than composite gaskets

thread_engagement.in_aluminum: Must use 1.5D engagement minimum due to lower shear strength

head_bolt_considerations.torque_sequence: Critical - must draw head down evenly

torque_to_yield.purpose: TTY bolts stretch consistently to maintain clamp load through thermal cycles
torque_to_yield.note: Single-use - do not reuse TTY head bolts

head_bolt_considerations.thermal_effects: Steel bolts expand less than aluminum head - clamp load increases at temperature

coolant_passage_alignment.concern: Differential expansion can misalign coolant passages
coolant_passage_alignment.design_solution: Oversized coolant holes with O-ring seals or elastomeric gaskets

head_resurfacing.combined_limit: Check manufacturer spec for total deck height variation

engines_using_this_interface: Chevrolet LS1/LS2/LS3 (aluminum heads, iron block options)
AMC 4.0L I6 with aftermarket aluminum head

aluminum_head_aluminum_block.description: All-aluminum construction - matched thermal expansion simplifies sealing

thermal_differential.engineering_impact: Matched expansion - head and block grow together

advantages: Head gasket sealing simplified - no differential movement
Consistent clamp load through thermal range

considerations.bore_interface: Still need wear-resistant bore surface (coating or liner)

engines_using_this_interface: All modern BMW with iron liners

steel_fastener_in_aluminum.description: Steel bolts threaded into aluminum - common throughout engines

thermal_differential.engineering_impact: Aluminum expands more than steel - affects clamp load at temperature

torque_considerations.cold_vs_hot: Clamp load INCREASES as assembly heats (aluminum grows, steel doesn't keep up)

anti_seize.required: YES - prevents galling between dissimilar metals

thread_locker.use_case: Only for fasteners not subject to thermal cycling
thread_locker.note: Thermal cycling can break thread locker bond

thread_engagement.thread_stripping: Aluminum threads fail first - size engagement for aluminum

retorque_requirements.initial_settle: Many aluminum assemblies require retorque after initial heat cycle

aluminum_piston_iron_bore.description: Aluminum piston in iron cylinder liner or iron block bore

cast_hypereutectic_4032.reason: Lower expansion = tighter cold clearance possible

forged_2618.reason: Higher expansion requires more clearance to prevent seizure

piston_to_wall_clearance.note: Piston expands MORE than bore - clearance decreases at temperature

skirt_design.purpose: Cam-ground and barrel-shaped to compensate for non-uniform expansion
skirt_design.expansion_struts: Some pistons have steel struts cast in to control skirt expansion

piston_rock_and_slap.cause: Excessive cold clearance causes piston slap on startup
piston_rock_and_slap.resolution: Balance between seizure prevention and NVH control

coatings.purpose: Reduce friction and wear during cold startup when clearances are largest

aluminum_piston_aluminum_bore.description: Aluminum piston in coated aluminum bore (Nikasil, Alusil, PTWA)

thermal_differential.engineering_impact: Much closer expansion rates than iron bore

nikasil.fuel_sensitivity: High sulfur fuel causes coating failure

alusil.ring_requirement: Ferrous or moly rings - must be harder than exposed silicon
alusil.break_in: Requires careful break-in to expose silicon crystals

galvanic_corrosion_matrix._description: Risk assessment for dissimilar metal contact in engine assemblies

torque_adjustment_factors._description: Torque modifications for material combinations and lubricants
torque_adjustment_factors.base_torque_for: Steel fastener in steel, clean and dry

combined_example.scenario: Steel bolt in aluminum with anti-seize
combined_example.calculation: Base torque × 0.85 × 0.80 = 68% of book torque for steel-in-steel dry

thermal_expansion_summary_table._units: ppm/K (parts per million per Kelvin, also written as μm/m·K)

quick_reference.note: Aluminum expands roughly twice as fast as iron - the fundamental challenge in hybrid engine construction
